subject: Embeddings latency surge following catalog sync — urgent customer impact
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@datapulse.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@datapulse.ai
Date: 2026-07-20T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Embedded vectors latency — sharp regressions after catalog push

Hi Rishi,

Putting this in writing — since the 02:00 UTC catalog sync on 2026-07-20 we've observed a sustained p95/p99 latency increase on the embeddings endpoint for our production workload (approx x3 at p95, x6 at p99). Throughput has dropped due to backpressure and we're seeing a 5% spike in 500 responses. This began immediately after your catalog update.

Attached a short latency graph and the service logs. Our SLAs are at risk for a handful of high-volume routes. Can you confirm whether you rolled a model variant or changed quantization profiles in the catalog? We need an immediate rollback or mitigation plan — our SRE team is standing by.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Platform, DataPulse

Attachments: latency_graph_20260722.png, svc_logs_20260722.zip

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@datapulse.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Embedded vectors latency — sharp regressions after catalog push

Evan — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. I see the graphs — this is unacceptable. I'm pulling the relevant folks now. Quick answers:
- We did a staggered catalog rollout at ~02:00 UTC that enabled a higher-throughput variant (quantized-8) for the embeddings model family in region us-east-1.
- There were no intentional routing policy changes.

Immediate plan: I will open an internal incident and propose a rollback to the prior catalog snapshot for your tenant routes.
Can you confirm which HubSpot deal ID I should quote when coordinating with your procurement/SLA teams?

I'll follow up in 15 with internal escalation notes.

— Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@datapulse.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T17:20:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Embeddings latency surge following catalog sync — urgent customer impact

Team — forwarding an urgent customer impact report from DataPulse. Key points:
- Impact: embeddings p95 ~3x, p99 ~6x, 5% increase in 500s for their production routes.
- Timeline: started immediately after our catalog sync (02:00 UTC, 2026-07-20).
- Suspected change: catalog enabled quantized-8 variant for embeddings; may have changed kernel selection / routing.

Requests:
1) Engineering (Markus) — can we validate the model variant rollout and kernel choices applied to customer's routes? If root cause is model variant, propose immediate rollback to previous catalog snapshot. Please estimate time to rollback and impact on other customers.
2) Product (Laura) — need a concise exec summary for a customer-facing statement and to coordinate with Sales leadership.
3) CS (Marissa) — please prepare a brief customer note acknowledging we've opened an incident and that we will follow with a timeline for mitigation within 2 hours.

I'll keep Evan in the thread for transparency. This needs exec visibility if rollback will affect other high-volume tenants.

On Thu, Jul 22, 2026 at 11:00 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rishi — ack. I'm triaging now. Initial telemetry shows increased decode latency on the new quantized kernels for sequence lengths typical of DataPulse's workload (avg 1024). We'll correlate with the kernel selection logs.
>
> I will comment asap on rollback feasibility.

— Rishi

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@datapulse.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T19:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Embeddings latency surge following catalog sync — urgent customer impact

Rishi / team — quick engineering summary:
- Root cause (preliminary): an aggressive kernel selection change for quantized-8 variants that chose a less optimal matmul path for long sequences. This increases per-token latency under high concurrency.
- Evidence: per-host kernel TL logs attached in svc_logs_20260722.zip.
- Mitigation options (ranked):
  1) Immediate rollback to catalog snapshot v20260719-2115 — fastest, low risk to other tenants if we scope to DataPulse routing rules first (estimated 30–45 min to roll back and validate).
  2) Hotfix in runtime to force the alternate matmul kernel for affected devices — likely 2–4 hours including testing.
  3) Interim rate-limit on customer routes to protect upstream services — seconds to apply but degrades customer throughput (requires CS/Legal sign-off for SLA impact).

Recommendation: rollback snapshot for DataPulse routing immediately, then schedule a full catalog rollback window and postmortem. If accepted, I will open change request INC-1134 and begin the rollback with SRE.

Attachments referenced: svc_logs_20260722.zip

— Markus
Director, Inference Engine

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@datapulse.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency surge following catalog sync — urgent customer impact

Evan — quick update and plan of record:

1) We will rollback your tenant routing to catalog snapshot v20260719-2115 scoped to your routes only. SRE + Markus will execute now (ticket: INC-1134). Estimated time to full validation: 30–45 minutes.

2) We'll follow with a customer-facing note from CS within 60 minutes summarizing impact and next steps; Laura will prepare the exec summary and I will join the call if you want live presence.

3) As a precaution we will open an account-level performance guard (soft rate-limiting) if the rollback shows residual stress; I will confirm before activating.

We understand the SLA risk and are treating this as priority-one. I'll share the incident link and a short write-up after rollback completes.

Thanks for your patience — we'll get this stabilized and follow with a root cause and remediation plan.

— Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
